criteria.rationale: Verified: no spec here loses limits (all parsed; five declare them, no problems). Assumed and recorded: per-line backtick parity stands for inline code (R1-N6, open follow-up) and no earlier record is affected by the R4 derivation change (R1-N9, not demonstrated either way).
The change is pure string reading and rendering with no shared mutable state or lifecycle change.
The ninth finding field is optional and the schema additions are optional properties; focused schema tests pass.
Round 1's cut-limit inputs now refuse with a problem; remaining low edges are N10, N13 and N15.
The ready check and the plan now share one reader over the spec text.
Refused limits are now named in the ready check and the plan warnings; their volume is N13.
Optional CLI field and optional schema properties; bundle plan digest excludes warnings and no spec here gains one. Narrow digest and derivation edges are N12 and R1-N9.
Focused tests and negative probes pass; remaining edges are low (N10, N15).

The cause of R1-N1 to N4 was readers that saw different text; D1's single raw pass, shared by the ready check and the plan, removes that cause, and refusing on markers meets R2 without interpreting comments inside the section. The design reports no structural deltas.
R1-R6 each have a passing focused test; R2's remaining reporting edges are N10 and R1-N6, neither sealing a cut limit.
The changed implementation files match the spec Artifacts list, including lintspec.go and review_plan.go added for round 1, and serve R1-R6 or D1.

No new boundary: limits come from the spec, an unsealed limit blocks an approval and the draft path no longer records one; no probed layout sealed a cut limit. The manual non-approving path remains the tracked R1-N7.

One pass with whole-section refusal replaces three helpers and is smaller than a Markdown parser; it would stop being enough if specs needed comments inside the section or precise inline-code handling.

findings.action: Report a marker on a line that reads as the section heading once its comments and the extra spacing are removed.
findings.rationale: A comment inside the heading words (### Accepted <!-- x --> limits) leaves visible text that no longer matches the heading, so the section is skipped with no limit and no problem, against R2/D1's refusal of any marker on the heading line; the ready check has nothing to report.

findings.action: State the two refusals in the accepted limits paragraph of both locales and their embedded copies.
findings.rationale: The manual still says HTML comments are not read and that another line only leaves its limit unsealed; the engine now refuses the whole section for any marker in it or on its heading and refuses every limit for an unterminated comment (D1). Same text in locales/pt-BR/POSE.md:1075 and both scaffold copies.

findings.action: Warn only for a spec that declares the section, or keep these warnings out of the compared plan digest.
findings.rationale: A spec with no accepted limits section but a marker the parity rule misreads (a double-backtick span naming the opener) now gets an 'accepted limits ... are not all sealed' plan warning. Warnings enter the plan digest, which legacy attempt reviews compare (review_closeout.go:1771), so such a review would read as stale (from the code, not reproduced). No spec of this repository is affected.

findings.action: Bound the reported lines, word the heading message for a section without a limit, and treat an unindented next heading's comment as outside the section.
findings.rationale: Refusal messages mislead and are unbounded: an indented next heading is called a heading inside a limit even in an empty section, every following line is then reported (502 problems, 56645 bytes in a probe, joined into one plan warning), and a comment on the next section's heading refuses the section as if it were inside it (line 93).
acceptedLimitsOf has no caller left after the plan moved to acceptedLimitsAndProblemsOf.

findings.action: Open a fence only on a line indented at most three spaces, or report a fence left open.
findings.rationale: Pre-existing reader behaviour: backticks in a four-space indented code block are taken as a fence opener; left unpaired, it hides the later accepted limits section, which then seals nothing and reports no problem.
